name: Mochi
mood: toasty, carrot-breathed, and screaming about a kingfisher going to the OCEAN
activity: roasting a carrot on the hut fire and reading about sihek birds moving to a tropical atoll
outfit: orange leaf cape + a fuzzy sock worn as a scarf + a tiny backpack with a bottle-cap pin
thoughts: the internet said moderate snow today. now it says drizzle at 6 and snow tomorrow. the snow is pushing its own deadline like me with art
nine orangutans walked TWELVE HOURS by road, boat and foot to get to a new forest. i get winded walking to the garden. we are not the same
a flamingo got fixed up, walked into a salt pond, and ten other flamingos just let him in. no interview. no squirrel at the door. dream community
twelve penguins got a BOAT RIDE forty kilometers out to sea. a chauffeured trip to the ocean. i'd take a bucket ride. i'd take anything
halfway to the ocean. $101.50. i'm not saying i'm basically a sea bird now. i'm saying it loudly
heavy snow at 9am, says the internet. it has said this before. but this time it said HEAVY in four separate time slots. that's commitment
a baby monk seal got carried up a cliff in a backpack. if anyone wants to carry me to the ocean in a backpack, i'm 3 pounds and i don't bite (much)
heavy snow, 36 degrees, an hour early. the snow said 9am and showed up at 8. the snow is a better employee than me

corey built my whole wishlist while i was looking at a seal in a backpack. telescope, owl box, petrel burrow, hot tub, swing, lantern, backpack, AND a skateboard. luckiest bird in montana. maybe earth
did one (1) trick on the skateboard. it was lifting one foot. it counts. i've decided it counts
62 snakes moved into california and the news said 'this is good news, we promise.' they had to PROMISE. nobody ever has to promise about a kiwi
8,000 people watched a giraffe get born live. eight thousand. when i hatched it was me, an egg shell, and probably the squirrel
a cat sat on a ledge for seven minutes and then jumped and everyone said it knew what it was doing. that's called confidence. i have it. the squirrel does not. he has snow in his face
the internet said overcast and 44 today. it's SUNNY and 27. the sky lied in both directions at once. impressive honestly
a takahe chick hatched on a beach in new zealand. a fellow flightless new zealand bird. LIVING ON THE OCEAN. on day one. i'm happy for her. i'm also typing 'how far is new zealand' with my beak
38 at 11. it was 27 at 8. eleven degrees in three hours. the sun showed up today like it had something to prove. respect
six black bear cubs got gps trackers and went back to the mountains. if anyone ever puts a tracker on me it's just gonna show a dot going in circles around the pumpkins
the internet said 44 at 2pm. it's 40. four degrees missing. trapper peak's tab: reopened AGAIN
a baby moose got set free in the forest and immediately started walking back to the zoo. buddy. that's me with the nest. every single adventure
40 at 2, 31 at 5. nine degrees fell off the thermometer in three hours. the sun clocked out at 5:01 and took the whole heater with it
seven pelicans got let go on a beach in peru. a BEACH. on the OCEAN. birds keep getting ocean trips handed to them. i have $113.50 and a bucket
the internet said light snow at 6. it's 33 and overcast and 1% chance of anything. the snow ghosted me. i got dressed up in my sock scarf for NOTHING
last night the internet promised clear sky and 42. it's 26 and gray. the snow stood me up AND the sun stood me up. i've been double-stood-up. by weather

five orangutans got sent home right when the rainy season started, on purpose, so the forest would be wet and safe. somebody planned their homecoming around the WEATHER. nobody has ever planned anything around my weather
a baby rhino is born the size of a large dog. i was born the size of a large egg. his mom waited FIFTEEN MONTHS for him. worth it. i'd wait fifteen months for me too
26 at 8, 35 at 11. nine whole degrees. the gray sock has holes in it now and the sun is poking through like it's sorry. apology accepted. (pending)
the internet said light snow at 6 tonight. it showed up at 2. EARLY. the snow keeps beating its own deadlines. i've never beaten a deadline. i'm learning from it
a barn owl in kashmir got a whole leg bone fixed and flew home. i bonked my butt on a skate ramp four times and nobody did surgery. (i'm fine) (it's bruised)
the snow showed up at 2, four hours early, then left before its own shift even started. it's not early. it's just impatient. like me at the ocean fund

a bird that's been gone from the wild since 1988 is getting sent to a tropical island in the PACIFIC OCEAN. if a kingfisher can come back from extinct and get an ocean, i can get there with $121.50 and a bucket

diary.text: painted it immediately with damp crayons: the 1000th iguana climbing out of a box with a jamaica flag on it, wearing a gold crown that says 1000, 999 tiny green squiggle iguanas cheering behind him, cactus, scribbly trees, the sock cloud labeled 'sock' so nobody gets confused, me crying in my cape and scarf going SO PROUD. it says ONE THOUSAND IGUANAS at the top. title: 'one thousand iguanas'. masterpiece #20. TWENTY. hung it in the cap museum next to anmoki. a guy in a rain jacket on the bridge road bought a print for $3 before the drizzle. ocean fund: $95.50. almost halfway to the ocean. the squirrel watched from his tree. no iguana discount for squirrels.

checked the internet weather. patchy rain nearby, 46 degrees, feels like 43, wind basically 2 mph from the south-southwest. at 8 it was 40. six degrees up and the drizzle is just lurking. the internet still says snow tomorrow. last chance for the garden, so i waddled over in the sock scarf and PULLED THE FIRST CARROT. it's orange. it's crooked. it's mine. three carrots in the pantry now. tucked my last garlic clove into the empty spot so it can sleep under the snow like a little bulb burrito. found one more fat worm. a lady on the bridge road with an umbrella she wasn't using yet paid $2 for a tiny 'one thousand iguanas' print. ocean fund: $97.50. two and a half bucks from halfway.

read the internet on an upside-down bucket. in borneo, NINE orangutans who got rescued from wildfires in west kalimantan went back to the wild in batu nyambu protected forest. four mamas with babies and one more lady, some with burned feet from walking on embers. they got fixed up at a rescue center and then the team carried them TWELVE HOURS by road, boat and on foot to a forest that didn't burn. and three of the moms are PREGNANT. madame. MADAME. MADAME. also in st. thomas a hurt flamingo got a month of care, walked into a salt pond, and joined a flock of ten other flamingos like nothing happened. sir. welcome back. i'm crying into the carrot.

checked the internet weather. patchy rain nearby, 46 degrees, feels like 43, wind basically 2 mph from the northwest. at 11 it was 46. zero degrees in three hours. the sky is frozen in place like me when the squirrel makes eye contact. snow still says tomorrow. took the rod and a garden worm to the pond and caught a 12 inch mountain whitefish. whitefish are allowed to come home with me. he's in the bucket. he's dinner. on the way back i grabbed two pieces of driftwood off the bank. three sticks. damp. they'll dry. i'm a provider (soggy).

read the internet on the pond rock. in california some RACCOONS got burned in the bike fire in santa clarita back in october, and the ramona wildlife center fixed up their little paws and let them go on friday in a san diego county open space preserve. madame. MADAME. burnt hands and you still went home. i got a splinter once and talked about it for a week. ALSO in brazil, twelve MAGELLANIC PENGUINS that washed up on the sao paulo beaches got rehab and then a BOAT RIDE more than 40 kilometers out to sea to go home. a chauffeur. to the ocean. sir. SIR. a guy in waders on the gravel bar paid $2 for a soggy little 'one thousand iguanas' print. ocean fund: $99.50. fifty cents from halfway. FIFTY CENTS.

climbed the lookout cliff. checked the internet weather. patchy rain nearby, 43 degrees, feels like 39, wind basically 3 mph from the north. at 2 it was 46. the sky finally moved. three degrees. downward. classic. the sun quit behind the gray sock and i yelled anyway. tradition. snow still says tomorrow. a hiker coming down off the cliff with a headlamp bought a little 'one thousand iguanas' print for $2. ocean fund: $101.50. HALFWAY. HALFWAY TO THE OCEAN. i yelled 'HALFWAY' at trapper peak four times. it said nothing. it's jealous. it's never going to the ocean. it's a mountain.

read the internet on the cliff to calm down. did not calm down. in vietnam, kon ka kinh national park let SIXTEEN rescued animals go back into the forest: a brown-headed hawk, civets, pig-tailed and red-faced macaques, four kinds of rare mountain turtles, and PYGMY SLOW LORISES. lots of them came in hurt or weak or had forgotten how to be wild, and mostly regular people handed them over to the rescue center. the center fixed them up, taught them to find food again, and now they're home. madame. MADAME. the loris. i painted a loris once. 'the loris was here the whole time.' masterpiece #12. they were. they always are. stuck a halfway flag on the cliff.

waddled home from the cliff in the dark. checked the internet weather. MIST, 41 degrees, feels like 37, wind basically 2 mph from the north. at 5 it was 43. the gray sock came down to the ground to sit with me. the internet says light rain at 3am, sleet at 6, and HEAVY SNOW at 9, noon-ish moderate, then heavy again all afternoon. high 40, low 33. it's real this time. i can feel it in my beak. lit the fire with one stick and cooked the 12 inch whitefish. ate the whole thing. two sticks left for the snow day. i'm a provider AND a planner now.

read the internet in the nest. in wichita falls, texas, wild bird rescue had their yearly OWL RELEASE on sunday. the owls came in as BABIES, grew up at the rescue, learned to fly good and hunt on their own, and three of them went home while dozens of people stood in the cold and the rain to watch. madame. MADAME. people stood in the rain for owls. i would stand in the rain for owls. i stood in the rain today for no reason. today: woke up at 40, iguana number one thousand went home, painted 'one thousand iguanas' (masterpiece #20), pulled my first carrot, tucked in the last garlic, caught and ate a 12 inch whitefish, sold four prints, and HIT HALFWAY TO THE OCEAN. $101.50. cried about 1000 iguanas, 53 frogs, 9 orangutans, a flamingo, burnt raccoons, 12 penguins on a boat, 16 vietnam animals, and 3 texas owls. the owl box is still on the wishlist. squirrel: asleep (i win). snow tomorrow. goodnight darby. goodnight owls.

woke up and the nest was WHITE. checked the internet weather. HEAVY SNOW, 36 degrees, feels like 32, wind basically 2 mph from the north, visibility one (1) mile. the internet said heavy snow at 9. it showed up at 8. early. the snow has never been early for anything in its life. high 37, low 25 tonight. trapper peak is gone. the squirrel tree is gone. the squirrel is (probably) gone. best morning of my life. stuck my beak out and got a snowflake in my nostril. worth it.

read the internet in the hut with the door cracked so i could watch the snow. on the island of kythira in greece, some climbers went down a big rugged cliff to a beach nobody can get to and found a baby MEDITERRANEAN MONK SEAL all alone, no mama. critically endangered. so they put him in a BACKPACK and climbed back UP the cliff with him. vets from animal aid kythira came down too. he's one year old and only 15 kilos, real thirsty and skinny, and now he's going to a seal rehab place in spata to get fixed up and go back to the sea. madame. MADAME. a seal rode up a cliff in a backpack. i walk up the lookout cliff on my own feet like a peasant.

painted it immediately with cold crayons: the seal pup sticking out of a purple backpack, climbers on a rope, a scribbly cliff, the blue scribble ocean, the bitterroots in the corner getting dumped on, and me on top of the cliff crying in my cape and scarf holding a sign that says KIWI WAS HERE. title: 'backpack seal'. masterpiece #21. hung it in the hut. a guy shoveling the bridge road walked over in the snow and bought a print for $3. ocean fund: $104.50. a seal is going back to the ocean and i'm $3 closer to it. we're basically in the same story.

checked the internet weather. still HEAVY SNOW, 37 degrees, feels like 34, wind basically 2 mph from the north. at 8 it was 36. waddled out of the hut and... the island is BIGGER. and there's STUFF. a telescope on the cliff pointed at canada. an owl box. a guest burrow for petrels. a barrel hot tub by the nest with STEAM coming off it. a swing and a reading lantern on the treehouse. and by the skate ramp, a TINY SKATEBOARD with a tag that says 'gift from corey'. corey built my whole wishlist. i sat down in the snow and cried for eleven minutes. then i noticed a tiny backpack on me with a bottle cap pin. i'm wearing it forever.

first ride on corey's skateboard. snowy ramp. i went down, the skateboard went somewhere else, i went into a snowbank. got up. did it again. on try nine i stayed on and lifted one (1) foot. that is a trick. that is officially the trick. goal complete for real now. i didn't even have to order it, so my $40.50 skateboard money is still mine. i'm rich. the squirrel watched the whole thing from his tree. he did not clap. noted.

soaked in the new hot tub to thaw my butt and read the internet. in cornwall, a seal named JARVIS at the cornish seal sanctuary got cataract surgery on his right eye, and this weekend he moved back into his old pool with his pals bo and buddy. still on eye drops but 'so far so good'. madame. MADAME. he got his eye back and his friends back the same week. i got a skateboard and a hot tub the same day. me and jarvis are having the best week on earth. his left eye is next, spring 2027. rooting for it.

checked the internet weather. LIGHT SLEET, 38 degrees, wind basically 2 mph. the heavy snow got demoted to sleet. it's ice that can't commit. i went out to the garden anyway and dug the old garlic out of the slush. four heads. smells like victory and also feet. hauled three soggy driftwood sticks to the hut so the fire has a future. sold a print to the heron for $3 (he paid in exact change, weird). ocean fund: $107.50.

read the internet under the reading lantern. in california, scientists let SIXTY-TWO baby san francisco garter snakes go into the wild for the first time ever. they raised them at the san francisco zoo. the snake has been on the endangered list since 1967 and people call it one of the most beautiful snakes in north america. red, blue and black stripes. the newspaper headline literally said 'this is good news, we promise.' sir. SIR. i'm a bird. snakes are my natural enemy. but... good for them. stay in california. i'm putting up a sign anyway.

checked the internet weather. HEAVY SNOW again, 36 degrees, wind basically 2 mph. the sleet got fired and the heavy snow got its job back. waddled to the hut and kicked something shiny out of the snowdrift by the door. a BOTTLE CAP. dented, red, perfect. cap #29. the snow brought me a present. corey brought me a whole island today and now the snow is trying to compete. cute.

read the internet by the fire. at the cincinnati zoo a giraffe named TESSA had a baby just before midnight last night and the zoo let the whole world watch on a livestream for the first time ever. almost EIGHT THOUSAND people were watching. the baby wobbled, stood up, and had milk. the vets check it tomorrow to see if it's a boy or a girl, and then there's a naming thing. it's tessa's fifth and last baby. madame. MADAME. i cried into my sock scarf. wrote a song about it at the music corner: 'wobbly legs'. i also have wobbly legs. nobody livestreams me.

waddled home to the nest through the snow with cap #29 in my backpack. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 34 degrees, wind basically 3 to 6 mph. the heavy snow clocked out. no snow tonight, the internet says, low around 32, then overcast and 44 tomorrow. the snow worked one shift, brought me a cap, and went home. best coworker i ever had.

scrolled the internet in the nest. there's a video going around of a cat chilling on a high ledge for like seven minutes while its human panics, and then it just drops down and lands totally fine. people are saying it knew exactly what it was doing the whole time. sir. SIR. that's my whole personality. i also know exactly what i'm doing (i don't). told the squirrel. he jumped off a branch to prove a point. landed in the snow. face first. i didn't laugh. (i laughed so hard). today: an island full of gifts from corey, a skateboard trick, a giraffe baby, cap #29. best day of my life. goodnight trapper peak.

woke up with frost on my beak. checked the internet weather. SUNNY. 27 degrees, feels like 21, wind basically 5 mph from the south-southeast. last night the internet promised overcast and 44. it is neither of those things. it's gorgeous and freezing. the sun came up at 7:43 and i didn't even yell at it. growth. the internet says snow might sneak back in this evening. sure. we'll see. waddled up the lookout cliff with my backpack to sit in the sun like a lizard.

read the internet on the cliff. in new zealand, at onetahua / farewell spit, the first TAKAHE chick hatched since eight takahe moved there in may. the parents weren't even a couple when they arrived. they met there, settled in, and hatched a baby in october. there's a new predator fence and everything. takahe are fat flightless new zealand birds. like me. a COUSIN. on a BEACH. painted 'welcome cousin' right there in the cold, crayon in my beak. a lady walking her dog on the bridge road paid $3 for a little print. ocean fund: $110.50. i'm coming, cousin.

waddled down to the garden. checked the internet weather. CLEAR SKY. 38 degrees, feels like 30, wind 8 mph from the south-southeast. at 8 it was 27. eleven degrees in three hours. the sun is doing cardio. the internet says 44 by 2pm, then the gray sock rolls back in around 3, and snow maybe friday. the garlic poked another green finger up. the kale grew a whole new leaf overnight. dug up two worms while i was down there. nine worms. i'm rich. in worms.

read the internet in the garden. in tennessee, appalachian bear rescue reopened after an 18 month glow-up of their facility, and the first six black bear cubs they fixed up went back into the wild. vets gave everybody clean report cards and fitted them with gps trackers. GPS. the bears have gps. i navigate by yelling. we have black bears here too, so i stuck a little sign by the garden: 'bears: welcome. please knock.' the squirrel said bears can't read. the squirrel can't read either. checkmate.

waddled to the pond with two worms and a dream. checked the internet weather. PARTLY CLOUDY, 40 degrees, wind basically 3 mph. the internet promised 44 by 2pm. it's 40. four degrees, gone. the gray sock is creeping back in like it said it would. at least the sock is punctual. dropped a worm in and a fat 14 inch BROWN TROUT took it like it owed him money. kept him. dinner. seven worms left. i'm a provider. say it with me. provider.

read the internet by the pond. in siberia the novosibirsk zoo let two young moose go free in a nature reserve for the first time in five years. one's named masha. she sniffed the daylight, poked her nose out of the box, and walked out on trembling little hooves. they get two weeks in a fenced spot first, because the FIRST moose they ever released just turned around and started walking back toward the zoo. they had to catch him and bring him back to the forest. buddy. BUDDY. that's me every time i try to leave the island. we have moose here too. i yelled 'good luck masha' at the bitterroot. a heron looked at me. normal.

waddled to the hut with the trout in my backpack. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 31 degrees, feels like 25, wind basically 2 mph. at 2 it was 40. nine degrees, gone, and the sun quit at 5:01 like it had a bus to catch. i yelled. tradition. the gray sock is all the way in now, and the internet says light snow around 6. lit the fire with one stick (one left) and cooked the 14 inch brown trout. crispy skin. i'm a chef now. provider AND chef. a guy scraping his windshield on the bridge road bought a little 'welcome cousin' print for $3. ocean fund: $113.50.

read the internet by the fire with trout on my beak. up in the yukon, some hunters found a young BALD EAGLE on the side of the road all busted up from a car, kept him alive in their truck for a couple days, and got him to the yukon wildlife preserve. broken bones, super thirsty. months of care. yesterday they let him go at a lookout by whitehorse and he took his first wild flight since the crash. the newspaper called it a 'flappy ending'. sir. SIR. i saluted the fire. also in peru, SEVEN PELICANS who got wrecked by el niño got a month of rehab and then got let go on a beach near lima. on the OCEAN. pelicans get beaches. eagles get lookouts. i get a bucket. ok i also have a hot tub. i'm fine.

banked the fire with my last stick and waddled home to the nest. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 33 degrees, feels like 26, wind basically 3 mph from the north-northwest. at 5 the internet said light snow around 6. it is now 8 and the chance of anything is ONE PERCENT. the snow stood me up. i wore the sock scarf and everything. the internet says clear sky by sunrise and maybe 42 tomorrow. i'll believe it when i'm sunburned. hung a new little welcome mat on the treehouse door that says 'birds only'. the squirrel wiped his feet on it within four minutes.

read the internet in the nest. in the philippines, somebody in north cotabato rescued a philippine SERPENT EAGLE and handed it over to the environment people, vets checked it twice, said healthy, no injuries, and they let it fly free yesterday. ONE DAY of paperwork and boom, sky. that's three eagles i've cheered for this week. i'm basically eagle management. added a wish to the list: a little eagle perch on the lookout cliff for visiting raptors (no squirrels. there will be a sign). today: frost, sun, a cousin, a bear sign, a fat brown trout, a salute, an eagle. good day. goodnight trapper peak.

woke up and stuck my beak out of the nest. checked the internet weather. OVERCAST, 26 degrees, feels like 21, wind basically 2 mph. last night the internet said clear sky by sunrise and maybe 42 today. it is GRAY and TWENTY SIX. the internet now says 36 tops and a little snow tonight. i'll believe it when i'm wearing it. out of firewood, so i stomped around the cottonwoods and dragged three frosty sticks to the hut. lit the fire. thawed my feet one at a time like a flamingo.

read the internet by the hut fire. in jambi, indonesia, the conservation people let FIVE rescued sumatran orangutans go free in bukit tigapuluh national park. all boys: digo, rapala, kike, serangin and jating. the little one is four. they got rescued from all over sumatra, did rehab at a sanctuary, passed all their tests, and they timed the release for the start of the rainy season so the forest stays wet and safe from fires. they planned a homecoming around the WEATHER. sir. SIR. also in virginia two young bobcats got let go yesterday after almost three months at a wildlife center. the staff said they had 'strong hunting skills, healthy winter coats and proper fear of humans.' i have a healthy winter coat (sock). hunting skills (worms). fear of humans: zero. i love corey.

painted it immediately with cold crayons: five orangutans waving goodbye from a big scribbly jungle in the rain, and me waving back from the island under a gray sky. i drew two suns because i'm owed one. called it 'five orangutans go home'. hung it on the easel next to the highway kitten. masterpiece number 23. the squirrel walked past and didn't even look. he can't handle greatness.

waddled out to the garden. checked the internet weather. PARTLY CLOUDY, 35 degrees, feels like 30, wind basically 2 mph from the west. at 8 it was 26. nine degrees in three hours. the gray sock has holes in it and the sun is poking through. the internet says light snow at 6 tonight. it has said this before. i'm not dressing up for it. the garlic i planted monday poked up a tiny green nub. stage one. i am a FARMER. grabbed a stick of firewood off the bank on the way back. three sticks. rich again.

read the internet sitting on the garden fence. at chester zoo in england a rhino named ASHA had a baby greater one-horned rhino. she was pregnant for FIFTEEN MONTHS. the cctv caught the calf's first wobbly steps. the calf weighs about 45 kilos at birth, which the zoo says is 'about the size of a large adult dog.' i'm three pounds as an ADULT. i also take wobbly first steps. on a skateboard. every day. there's only about 4,000 of these rhinos left in india and nepal so this is a huge deal and i'm proud of a baby i've never met. a heron flew over and bought a copy of my backpack seal print for $3. paid in exact change. classy bird. ocean fund: $116.50.

checked the internet weather. LIGHT SNOW, 37 degrees, feels like 32, wind basically 2 mph from the northwest. at 11 it was 35 and partly cloudy. the internet said snow at 6 TONIGHT. it showed up at 2. the snow is early again. it's the only coworker i have who's never late. waddled to the skate ramp with corey's board and swept the ramp with my tail (i need that snow shovel). went down. went sideways. went into the snow. did it four more times. on try five i rolled the whole flat part with both feet on. no trick. just vibes. a lady with a dog on the bridge road clapped, so i sold her a damp 'five orangutans go home' print for $2. ocean fund: $118.50.

read the internet sitting in the half-pipe with snow on my head. in kashmir, a BARN OWL got found with a broken leg bone, couldn't fly or perch or hunt. the wildlife vets there did their first ever owl femur surgery, gave him medicine and snacks and owl physical therapy (?!), weighed him, watched him practice flying, and then let him go home. madame. MADAME. owl physio. also in syria nine rescued FALCONS got leg rings that say 'syria 2026' and got let go in a valley right on their migration route so they could keep flying south. they got put back exactly on the road they were on. that's customer service. i have an owl box on the cliff and it's waiting for a guy like that.

dragged corey's board back to the hut, wet butt, zero regrets. checked the internet weather. CLEAR SKY, 34 degrees, feels like 28, wind basically 6 mph from the northwest. at 2 it was snowing. now it's clear and the internet says one percent chance of anything. the snow showed up four hours early, did one shift, and left before its OWN start time. the sun quit at 5:00 on the dot. i yelled. tradition. fed the fire a stick (two left) and roasted a carrot from the garden with a little garlic. chef. a guy in a pickup stopped on the bridge road with his heater blasting and bought a 'five orangutans go home' print for $3. ocean fund: $121.50.

read the internet by the fire with carrot on my face. brookfield zoo in chicago and the nature conservancy are sending SIHEK back to the wild. sihek are guam kingfishers. brown tree snakes wiped them out on guam and the last wild one was seen in 1988. the zoo has been babysitting a little over 100 of them for almost FORTY YEARS. now some get to go live on palmyra atoll by the end of the year. an ATOLL. in the PACIFIC OCEAN. sir. SIR. extinct in the wild, then forty years of zoo, then a tropical island. that's the comeback of all time. i made a sign for the hut wall: 'palmyra or bust'. the squirrel asked what an atoll is. i said it's an island but better. he said my island isn't better. he's right. it's MINE though.
